ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: For Hong Kong: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615), Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) including significant controllers register requirements, Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310), and the Companies Registry and Hong Kong Monetary Authority AML/CFT guidelines. For any mainland China ultimate beneficial owner or parallel mainland registration: PBOC and SAMR Order No. 3 (Measures for Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Administration of Customer Due Diligence and Preservation of Client Identity Materials and Transaction Records), effective 1 November 2024.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Hong Kong Companies Registry (or, for a mainland China foreign-invested partnership, the State Administration for Market Regulation issuing the Foreign-Invested Partnership Business License)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the High Court Registry of Hong Kong if the document originates from or is destined for an Apostille Convention state; otherwise, notarization followed by consular legalization at the relevant consulate or embassy for non-Apostille states. The apostille and consular legalization paths are parallel and mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Hong Kong Companies Registry for the Hong Kong entity, or the originating companies registry for any foreign parent or partner entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the designated competent authority in the issuing jurisdiction when the destination state is an Apostille Convention member; alternatively, notarization plus consular legalization at the destination jurisdiction's diplomatic mission for non-member states. The two methods are mutually exclusive and sequential chaining of apostille and consular legalization is prohibited.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors or authorized management committee of the parent entity, general partner, or designated formation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized execution and Hague Apostille issued by the appropriate competent authority (such as the China Ministry of Foreign Affairs or an authorized provincial foreign affairs office for mainland China documents) if the destination is an Apostille Convention state; for non-Apostille destinations, notarization followed by consular legalization by the destination state's consulate. These are alternative, non-cumulative authentication paths.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry or the constituent shareholders and partners executing the constitutional document and, where applicable, the partnership agreement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified true copy notarized and authenticated by Hague Apostille in the country of issuance when the receiving jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention member; otherwise, notarization and consular legalization at the destination jurisdiction's embassy or consulate. No hybrid or sequential use of both authentication regimes is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: A licensed financial institution such as an HKMA-authorized bank maintaining the FIP's principal operating or franchise royalty account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Signature notarization and Hague Apostille by the competent authority of the document's origin state for use in an Apostille Convention jurisdiction; for non-member jurisdictions, notarize the bank officer's signature and obtain consular legalization from the destination state. The two regimes are exclusive alternatives and must never be chained.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, partners, general partners, natural-person beneficial owners, signatories, and authorized agents against the Hong Kong HKSAR police and regulatory freeze lists, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, the United Nations Security Council sanctions lists, EU and UK consolidated sanctions lists, and domestic PRC restricted-party and undesirable-entity lists issued by MOFCOM and the Ministry of State Security must be completed before execution of any formation document. Enhanced due diligence with full source-of-funds and source-of-wealth documentation is required for politically exposed persons, their family members, close associates, and any FIP expected to make large franchise royalty wire transfers. Screening must be repeated at least every 24 hours during the formation period and re-run immediately upon any new sanctions designation, with all negative or positive findings documented in a timestamped compliance desktop file.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Hong Kong Companies Registry e-Search and Integrated Companies Registry Information System (ICRIS), together with Business Registration Office name checks under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310); if the FIP is registered in mainland China, the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) name reservation and notification system applies.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Hong Kong permits an English name and an optional traditional Chinese name; the Chinese name must be a phonetic or idiomatic transliteration of the English name and must not exceed the prescribed token set or create confusion with existing registered names. For mainland China registration, the four-tier naming convention must be observed: administrative division, trade name, industry description, and organizational form. Any English franchise name must be matched to a Mandarin pinyin transliteration where required by the SAMR business license, and the name must not contain vocabulary implying government affiliation, regulated financial business, or protected geographical indications without ministerial approval.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a name rejection, the applicant must obtain the written refusal notice and, within 30 days, request an administrative review through the Hong Kong Companies Registry under the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) or through the SAMR name review procedure if the FIP is registered in mainland China. The appeal package must include the original proposed name, the registry reference number, a revised compliant name where appropriate, and legal submissions distinguishing the mark from existing names, prohibited tokens, or misleading elements. If refusal is based on statutory prohibition, the applicant may submit evidence of prior registration, consent letters, acquired distinctiveness, or official authorization from the relevant minister. To preserve the franchise timeline, a fresh name reservation application should be filed concurrently, and an unsuccessful administrative appeal may be escalated to the Administrative Appeals Board or a competent court in accordance with the governing procedural law.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A Hong Kong FIP or company must maintain a physical registered office in Hong Kong capable of receiving statutory documents and service of process; a bare virtual office, commercial mail-forwarding address, or post office box will not satisfy the Companies Ordinance or the Business Registration Ordinance. HKMA-supervised banks and the Inland Revenue Department generally reject virtual-only addresses for franchise royalty collection accounts and tax registration because they do not demonstrate commercial substance. For the boba tea global franchise model, the entity must maintain a genuine physical address, local management or authorized representative, business records, and bank account in Hong Kong. If the FIP is instead registered in mainland China, SAMR and the local tax authorities likewise require a real operating address and will not accept a virtual mailbox. A serviced office with dedicated physical workspace and staffed reception may be acceptable, but only if it is a real leased space and not a mere accommodation venue.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) registered office is staffed or accessible during business hours; (2) entity name is displayed outside the premises; (3) statutory records, partnership agreement, business license, and bank KYC files are kept at the registered office; (4) the beneficial ownership register is available to the competent government authority; (5) a local compliance officer is appointed to respond to Companies Registry, IRD, and HKMA inquiries; (6) the address is not a post office box or mail-forwarding box. Quantified risk: unannounced physical on-site inspections by Hong Kong Companies Registry, Inland Revenue Department, and HKMA authorized officers are moderate for a cross-border franchise FIP with royalty wire flows, with an estimated likelihood of 35-45 percent during the first year of operation and higher probability if turnover anomalies or suspicious transaction reports arise. In mainland China, SAMR and tax authorities conduct targeted on-site inspections at a 50-65 percent probability when a foreign-invested partnership is used as an intellectual property holding and royalty vehicle without demonstrated local commercial substance.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Limited Partnerships Ordinance (Cap. 37) of Hong Kong SAR, particularly sections 4, 5, and 7; Partnership Ordinance (Cap. 38) for general provisions; Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) for foreign company registration if applicable.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Hong Kong Companies Registry, Limited Partnerships Section
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Limited Partnership (Form LP1)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is required for a limited partnership in Hong Kong. However, the partnership agreement must specify the capital contributions of each partner. No escrow account is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE PARTNERS OF [PARTNERSHIP NAME] (the 'Partnership') ADOPTED BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT IN LIEU OF A MEETING ON [DATE]. WHEREAS, the Partnership was formed under the Limited Partnerships Ordinance (Cap. 37) of Hong Kong SAR on [Date of registration]; and WHEREAS, the Partners desire to adopt certain resolutions to govern the initial operations and administration of the Partnership. NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS: 1. CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION: The Partners hereby ratify and subscribe to the capital contributions as set forth in the Partnership Agreement, and each Partner shall contribute the amounts specified therein to the Partnership's capital account. The General Partner is authorized to call for such contributions as may be required for the conduct of the Partnership's business. 2. REGISTERED OFFICE: The registered office of the Partnership shall be located at [Address], and the Partnership hereby adopts such address as its official registered office for all statutory and legal purposes. The General Partner is authorized to file any necessary documents with the Companies Registry to reflect this designation. 3. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: The Partners hereby authorize the opening of bank accounts in the name of the Partnership with [Bank Name] and any other financial institutions as the General Partner may deem necessary. The General Partner and any designated signatories are hereby authorized to execute all banking documents, including but not limited to account opening forms, deposit agreements, and withdrawal instructions, and to manage the Partnership's funds in accordance with the Partnership Agreement. 4. APPOINTMENT OF OFFICERS: The Partners hereby appoint [Name] as the General Partner and [Name] as the Designated Representative for the purpose of compliance with the Business Registration Ordinance and other statutory requirements. The General Partner shall have full authority to manage the day-to-day operations of the Partnership, subject to the limitations set forth in the Partnership Agreement. 5. GENERAL AUTHORITY: The General Partner is hereby authorized to execute all such documents, take all such actions, and do all such things as may be necessary or desirable to carry out the foregoing resolutions and to comply with all applicable laws and regulations of Hong Kong SAR. 6. EFFECTIVENESS: These resolutions shall be effective immediately and shall remain in full force and effect until amended or revoked by a subsequent resolution of the Partners. This resolution is executed as of the date first written above. [Signature of General Partner] [Signature of Limited Partner]

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Hong Kong Companies Registry - Cyber Registry Centre
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search on the Cyber Registry Centre to ensure the proposed partnership name is not identical or too similar to an existing entity. If available, submit an application for name reservation via the e-Registry portal. The name must end with 'Limited' or 'L.P.' as appropriate. Provide the proposed name and a brief description of the business nature. The reservation is valid for three months. Ensure compliance with the Limited Partnerships Ordinance and the Companies Ordinance.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to similarity, submit an alternative name or appeal to the Registry with justification within 14 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Hong Kong Companies Registry - Limited Partnerships Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form LP1 (Application for Registration of a Limited Partnership) and submit it to the Companies Registry along with the prescribed fee. The form must be signed by all partners. Include the partnership agreement, which must detail the rights and obligations of partners, capital contributions, and profit-sharing arrangements. The application must be filed within 14 days of the partnership's formation. The Registry will issue a Certificate of Registration upon approval.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, respond to the Registry's inquiries within 14 days. If rejected, correct the deficiencies and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department - Business Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of the partnership's registration, apply for a Business Registration Certificate. Submit the completed Form IRC1 (Application for Business Registration) along with the registration fee. The certificate must be displayed at the business premises. The registration is valid for one year and must be renewed annually. Ensure that the business name matches the registered partnership name.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is delayed, contact the Business Registration Office to expedite. If the application is rejected, correct the information and reapply.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of Statutory Officers and Registered Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure that the partnership has a registered office in Hong Kong and that the General Partner and any Designated Representative are properly appointed. File any changes with the Companies Registry using Form LP2 (Change of Particulars) if necessary. The registered office must be a physical address, not a post office box. The partnership must maintain a register of partners and a copy of the partnership agreement at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as General Partner
Consent to act as Designated Representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry requires additional information, provide it within 14 days. If the registered office is not compliant, provide an alternative address.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Banking Authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial banks in Hong Kong (e.g., HSBC, Standard Chartered)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account in the name of the partnership. Provide the Certificate of Registration, Business Registration Certificate, partnership agreement, and identification of all partners. The bank will conduct due diligence and may require a resolution authorizing the opening of the account. Ensure that the banking authorization resolution is included as per the first resolution. The bank may require a personal interview with the General Partner.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the application, provide additional documentation or choose another bank. If the bank requires a personal interview, schedule it promptly.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Food and Environmental Hygiene Department (FEHD) of Hong Kong SAR; Environmental Protection Department (EPD) for environmental matters
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Business License (for storage and distribution of syrups and food ingredients)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Department (EPD) of Hong Kong SAR
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - No EIA required as the business does not involve manufacturing or large-scale industrial activities. However, if the storage of chemicals or hazardous substances exceeds thresholds, a Chemical Waste Producer Registration may be required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable. The business must comply with the Food Business Regulation (Cap. 132X) regarding hygiene and storage conditions. No specific discharge or emissions standards apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification for the storage premises is required under the Fire Services Ordinance (Cap. 95). The premises must pass a fire safety inspection and obtain a Fire Safety Certificate. Additionally, the Occupational Safety and Health Ordinance (Cap. 509) requires a safe working environment; a workplace safety inspection may be required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: For the PRC sovereign territory: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China, accessible through the STA Electronic Tax Bureau and the national electronic invoice service platform. For the Hong Kong SAR sub-jurisdiction: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), including the Business Registration Office, accessible through GovHK and the IRD e-Tax electronic filing portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: PRC leg: The Foreign-Invested Partnership (FIP) first obtains its Unified Social Credit Code (USCC) business license from the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR). The USCC constitutes the statutory tax identification number (TIN) for PRC tax administration. The FIP must then complete tax registration through the STA Electronic Tax Bureau within 30 days after issuance of the business license, selecting the competent tax authority office, activating the VAT and income tax filing modules, and establishing electronic invoice rights. Hong Kong leg: The FIP must apply for Business Registration under the Business Registration Ordinance with the IRD Business Registration Office within one month of commencing business in Hong Kong, resulting in the issuance of a Business Registration Certificate and Business Registration Number (BRN). The BRN serves as the Hong Kong tax identification reference. Non-resident partners are not required to obtain separate PRC TINs unless a PE or withholding obligation arises; for Hong Kong Profits Tax, non-resident partners carrying on business in Hong Kong are assessable in their individual capacities on their partnership shares, with the partnership filing obligations administered through the IRD.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Neither the PRC nor Hong Kong SAR provides check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections for this entity type. The FIP is mandatorily treated as a pass-through arrangement for PRC enterprise income tax and Hong Kong profits tax; profits are allocated to partners for tax at partner level. No entity-level tax classification election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT in mainland China; Hong Kong SAR has no general VAT, GST, or sales and use tax, but imposes duties on selected excisable goods and charges a business registration fee.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: PRC VAT: there is no turnover threshold for initial VAT/tax registration; the mandatory general VAT taxpayer threshold is RMB 5,000,000 of annual taxable sales, above which the FIP must register as a general VAT taxpayer and charge output VAT at applicable rates (13% for goods, 6% for services, 9% for certain categories). Hong Kong SAR: no indirect-tax registration threshold exists because no VAT is imposed; business registration is compulsory upon commencement of business irrespective of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: PRC: The fully digitalised electronic invoice system is mandatory on the STA national electronic invoice service platform; special VAT invoices and digital e-invoices must be transmitted in real time to the tax authority for automatic verification and anti-fraud digital encryption, with API connectivity required under the Golden Tax Phase IV environment. Hong Kong SAR: no real-time fiscal clearance, no mandatory API-based e-invoicing system, and no digital stamping requirement; invoices are issued voluntarily without pre-clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: PRC: exported goods, including bubble-tea syrups, concentrates, and physical franchise supply-chain goods sold to overseas franchisees, qualify for the 0% export VAT rate and eligible input-VAT rebate when the goods physically depart mainland China, export customs procedures are completed, title passes to a non-resident buyer, and the foreign-exchange proceeds are repatriated through a designated PRC bank. Cross-border franchise licensing and related services supplied to a recipient located outside mainland China and wholly consumed outside mainland China may also be zero-rated or treated as outside the charging scope of PRC VAT, subject to the statutory documentation set. Hong Kong SAR: no VAT/GST exists, so export zero-rating is not a Hong Kong requirement.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (customs bill of entry) endorsed by PRC Customs with a valid declaration serial number
Commercial invoice and digital e-invoice or special VAT invoice issued to the overseas franchisee
Bill of lading or air waybill evidencing physical export movement from mainland China
Packing list, export contract, certificate of origin, and product specification documentation
Bank foreign-exchange receipt confirmation / export proceeds collection record from a PRC designated foreign-exchange bank evidencing repatriation of proceeds
Franchise licensing contract, service description, payment receipt, and evidence of offshore consumption for zero-rated cross-border services
Tax-residence certificate or non-resident status evidence of the overseas franchisee where required by the VAT zero-rating or export-rebate dossier
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: PRC: Tax authorities, PRC Customs, and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange jointly audit zero-rating and export-rebate claims. Any missing customs, transport, invoice, or foreign-exchange repatriation evidence invalidates the 0% rate and re-classifies the supply as taxable at the applicable VAT rate; claimed input-credit rebates are recovered together with late-payment interest. Deliberate export-tax-rebate fraud triggers recovery of the entire rebate, a monetary penalty of one to five times the defrauded tax amount, suspension or revocation of export-rebate qualification, and criminal prosecution under PRC Criminal Law Article 204. Hong Kong SAR: no VAT zero-rating regime exists, so no VAT clawback penalty arises; however false or incorrect profits tax declarations are subject to IRD additional assessments, penalties up to three times the tax undercharged, and criminal prosecution for tax evasion.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) as the competent PRC foreign-exchange control authority
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The PRC maintains a managed floating RMB regime with current-account convertibility for genuine trade and services, but all capital-account transactions remain stringently controlled by PBOC/SAFE. For an onshore China Foreign-Invested Partnership (FIP), RMB is freely usable for operating receipts and payments that are supported by genuine underlying contracts, including franchise royalty receivables, syrup export income, rent, payroll, supplier invoices and tax. Cross-border capital receipts such as partnership capital contributions, shareholder loans, and foreign-exchange conversion of equity are not freely convertible: the FIP must complete SAFE FDI-capital registration with the designated bank, use an approved capital-account facility, and observe positive-list disbursement rules. Profit repatriation and dividend/liquidation distributions are current-account remittances only after audited financials, capital verification, tax clearance/withholding evidence and the underlying partnership profit distribution resolution are lodged; PRC withholding tax generally at 10% for non-residents, subject to tax treaty reduction, must be paid and evidenced. Significant structural hurdles remain for early redemption, premature liquidation, assignment of partnership interests, and round-tripped investments, which require prior SAFE approval, fair-value certification, and special interbank payment codes. Thus, the currency is operationally convertible but strategically reserved.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under SAFE trade-forex administration, an FIP exporting boba syrup and related ingredients must repatriate export foreign-currency receipts to its PRC designated bank accounts in accordance with the underlying contract; where the expected receipt date is later than 90 days after customs declaration, the FIP must register a deferred collection with the Trade Forex Monitoring System before the original maturity. The default statutory collection cap is 90 days from customs declaration for goods exports, unless extended and justified by commercial terms. There is no mandatory fixed surrender ratio or mandatory conversion percentage: the FIP may choose between retaining the foreign currency in its export collection account or settling to RMB at the onshore spot rate. The bank will perform truthfulness verification through electronic trade records, customs data, contracts and invoices before allowing conversion or payment.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Viability is Low and materially restricted for the onshore PRC FIP. Offshore digital EMIs such as Airwallex, Currencycloud, N26 and similar are not licensed by SAFE/PBOC to maintain foreign-exchange or RMB settlement accounts for PRC domestic or foreign-invested entities. They cannot receive approved FDI capital injections nor execute SAFE trade verification and payment declaration. An onshore FIP may only use a domestic designated bank or a domestic joint-stock bank with an FX derivatives license for trade and capital flows. The HK parent, if separately established, may use HK-licensed virtual banks or EMIs for its own offshore liquidity, but those rails must not be commingled with the PRC entity's export proceeds, capital account or royalty settlement. A pragmatic hybrid is to use onshore Tier-1 bank accounts for all PRC FIP flows and a separate HK treasury account for the investor, with intercompany transfers documented as arm's length payments.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: PRC regulations require the legal representative or a formally authorized responsible person to appear physically before the domestic bank's compliance team for the opening of a corporate RMB basic deposit account and every foreign exchange capital/trade account. Remote-only consent, including a consular proxy, is not generally accepted for the statutory face-to-face KYC interview. If the legal representative is outside China, the FIP is strongly advised to have the legal representative and the proposed signatory attend a PRC notarized power-of-attorney ceremony at the Chinese embassy or consulate; afterwards, the authorized financial officer must still travel to the branch in person with original passport, POA and corporate seals for the interview. Some provinces have remote video dual-control pilots for small enterprises, but a foreign-invested partnership with cross-border capital flows will almost invariably be classified as higher-risk and subjected to an in-branch interview, site visit and transaction expected-revenue benchmarking.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent beneficial ownership chain: the FIP has HK corporate partners or limited partners, creating uncertainty over the individuals who ultimately own or control the partnership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full partnership deed and English/Chinese notarized translations; complete register of general and limited partners; constitutional documents including Certificate of Incorporation, Memorandum and Articles of Association and shareholder registers for every HK corporate partner; HK Business Registration and Companies Registry search reports; source-of-wealth statements together with bank statements covering at least 12 months for each natural person owning 25% or more; and an organizational chart with percentage ownership, nationality and PEP status.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering red flag in the syrup franchise supply chain: identical goods shipped with fluctuating unit prices, missing freight and insurance evidence, or royalty payments not proportionate to store counts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master franchise agreements and regional sub-franchise contracts; notarized price schedule and transfer pricing policy benchmarked under OECD TNMM; authentic commercial invoices, packing lists, bills of lading or air waybills, customs export declarations, certificates of origin; and a royalty calculation ledger tied to royalty reports from franchisee POS systems or audited store-count reports.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border capital injection into the FIP fails source-of-funds trace: contributed monies arrive from a Hong Kong pooling account or a non-banking intermediary, not directly from the stated investor.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Direct SWIFT MT103 traceability evidence including original payment instructions from the investor's HK corporate bank account; audit reports and HK tax filings covering the proposed funds; board resolution or partnership capital call approving the injection; SAFE FDI/FIP foreign exchange registration certificate or online filing proof; and confirmation that all participants are not sanctioned or restricted.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Profit repatriation and royalty outflows to Hong Kong trigger tax evasion or informal remittance risks: materially high royalty payments when the franchise business is low-profit or appears fabricated.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered license and trademark portfolio in the PRC and HK; IP license agreement with a written royalty formula applied to gross revenue and commercial restrictions economically substantiated; PRC withholding tax payment voucher and invoice issued for the royalty; evidence of actual use of IP by the franchisee; audited P&L of the FIP confirming arm's length residual profit; and a notarized undertaking from the HK beneficiary confirming no round-tripping.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: After SAFE has registered the FIP as a Foreign-Invested Partnership and the investor has completed the state-assigned annual reporting via the market supervisory authority, the foreign partner must open an onshore Foreign Exchange Capital Account at a designated bank. The remitting bank in Hong Kong must instruct a SWIFT MT103 with beneficiary account naming the FIP's capital account, beneficiary bank SWIFT/BIC, purpose code corresponding to Direct Investment Capital Contribution in the SAFE International Balance of Payments transaction classification, and the SAFE-FDI registration reference number in the beneficiary-to-info field. The PRC receiving bank credits the FX capital account, performs a verifiable receipt declaration and then, upon presentation of the FIP's business license, partnership agreement and investor resolution, allows conversion to RMB and transfer to the RMB basic account strictly for positive-list permitted purposes including wages, raw materials, rent, taxes and operating expenses. The external auditor should issue a capital verification report only when required by the partnership agreement; there is no statutory minimum capital, but the actual contribution must be remitted from the overseas investor's own account and cannot be advanced by an unrelated third party.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: All outbound settlement must be routed through the FIP's onshore FX settlement account using domestic bank payment rails, not offshore EMIs. For standard high-value supplies and franchise inventory purchases from third-party suppliers, use SWIFT MT103 with purpose code Trade Payment or Goods Import and supporting invoice, contract, proforma invoice, bill of lading and customs record. If the FIP is importing tea, milk powder or packaging from a Hong Kong or offshore supplier, an irrevocable confirmed at-sight Letter of Credit is recommended: the FIP applies through its Tier-1 bank, the L/C is advised and negotiated through the beneficiary's bank, and the corresponding HKD or USD settlement is executed on presentation of compliant documents. For recurring low-ticket shipments of syrups and franchise supplies from mainland to related franchisee stores in Hong Kong, a Documentary Collection at sight or with tenor is permitted and provides control over shipping documents while avoiding open-account risk to the franchisee. In every case SAFE current-account trade authenticity checks apply: the FIP must retain the underlying contract, customs declaration where applicable, invoice and bank payment application referencing the same invoice number, and must register in the Trade Forex Monitoring System.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable CNY forward foreign exchange contracts against USD or HKD for genuine current-account receipts and payments
Cross-currency swap for approved current-account or foreign-currency borrowing cashflows, subject to real trade background and maturity matching
RMB foreign exchange options with an onshore designated bank to hedge uncertainty of royalty receipts, covered by real exposures and not leveraged
Offshore non-deliverable forward for the HK parent only; the PRC FIP is not permitted to transact NDFs onshore because SAFE requires actual delivery

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Business Registration Renewal and Levy Payment under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department – Business Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the expiry date shown on the current Business Registration Certificate, typically 31 March for calendar-year businesses or the anniversary of commencement for new registrations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal attracts a HK$300 late fee; continued non-payment can lead to a summons, a maximum fine of HK$5,000 plus a daily default fine, and ultimately deregistration or strike-off from the Business Register

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Partnership Profits Tax Return (Form BIR52) and Supplementary Partnership Schedule S2
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), Profits Tax Section
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month from the date of issue of the return; where issued after the annual Profits Tax returns release (normally the first working day of April), an extension to the specified deadline may be granted only through filing via eTAX or a recognised tax representative
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file by the required date enables the IRD to issue an estimated assessment; defaulters are liable to a fine of up to HK$10,000 and additional assessed tax of up to 3 times the amount undercharged under Cap. 112 s. 82

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer's Annual Return of Remuneration and Pensions (Forms BIR56A and IR56B) for each employee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after the end of the year of assessment; the prescribed filing cycle is by 30 April for the immediately preceding 31 March year of assessment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing is an offence punishable by a fine of up to HK$10,000; where tax is underpaid, the IRD may assess additional tax up to 3 times the tax avoided

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Certified Audited Financial Statements (or Accountants' Report) attached to the Partnership Profits Tax Return when statutory thresholds are exceeded
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department (attached to Form BIR52); retained at the registered office for inspection by the Commissioner
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due with the Profits Tax Return: normally within 1 month of the issue date, or the extended deadline for tax representatives (commonly 15 to 30 days after the original due date); financial statements must be made up to the accounting date of the FIP
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to attach audited accounts renders the return defective; the IRD may issue a default assessment, impose a 5% default charge on tax undercharged, and initiate prosecution under Cap. 112 s. 82 with fines of up to HK$10,000 and additional tax of 3 times the undercharge

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Food Business / Restaurant Licence Renewal (if the franchise entity directly operates a boba tea outlet; otherwise not applicable to pure franchisor licensing activity)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Renewal application must be submitted before the expiry date printed on the current licence; FEHD usually sends renewal notices 60 days before expiry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Operation without a renewed licence is an offence punishable by a maximum fine of HK$20,000 and 3 months' imprisonment; continued unlicensed operation may result in closure of the food premises

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A certified independent CPA audit is mandatory in Hong Kong when: (1) the entity is a private company that fails the small entity audit exemption under Cap. 622 s. 359, i.e. it exceeds at least two of the three thresholds of annual revenue HK$10 million, total assets HK$10 million, and 50 employees; or (2) the partnership's gross income in a year of assessment exceeds HK$5 million, requiring certified financial statements under the Inland Revenue Ordinance; or (3) the franchise agreement, bank facility, or cross-border clearance process requires an audited balance sheet irrespective of local statutory exemption.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS) as issued by the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants, equivalent to IFRS; HKFRS for Private Entities (SME Framework) is permitted for eligible small private entities under HKICPA standards

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Hong Kong does not impose a publicly filed UBO annual return. The FIP must maintain a Significant Controllers Register and, if it is a limited partnership, a Register of Partners at its registered office; any change in significant controllers or partners must be recorded within 7 days and any transfer of partnership interest affecting the registered particulars must be filed with the Companies Registry within 30 days under the Limited Partnership and Companies (Records) requirements. For corporate franchise subsidiaries, share transfers must be recorded in the Register of Members immediately and reflected in the next Annual Return (NAR1) filed within 42 days after the anniversary date.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 to USD 1,200 per annum depending on the registered-agent venue, corporate secretarial service scope and supplementary UBO/AML/KYC administration
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000 to USD 8,000 per annum for a certified independent audit under HKFRS; USD 1,200 to USD 3,500 for an accountants' report/review for a small pass-through partnership

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The PRC Foreign-Invested Partnership (FIP) itself is fiscally transparent and is not a Corporate Income Tax (CIT) taxpayer. CIT is imposed at the partner level. A resident corporate partner is taxed at the standard 25% rate, subject to reductions: 15% for High and New Technology Enterprises; 15% for qualifying Western China encouraged industries; 20% reduced rate for small low-profit enterprises on qualifying income; 100% additional deduction for eligible R&D expenses; and exemption for qualifying treasury bill interest and certain dividend income derived between PRC resident enterprises. The Hong Kong corporate partner may also enjoy the Mainland-Hong Kong Double Tax Arrangement (DTA) reduced withholding rates on profit repatriation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: PRC Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return (Form A100000) plus Basic Information Schedule (A000000), reconciliation schedules (A105000 series), loss carryforward schedule (A106000), and tax treaty benefit schedule (A107011), filed through the State Taxation Administration electronic tax bureau portal by the corporate partner of the FIP.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual with quarterly provisional payments; non-resident withholding tax filings are event-driven upon each profit repatriation payment.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual CIT return is due by 31 May following the tax year-end; quarterly provisional CIT prepayments are due within 15 days after each calendar quarter-end; non-resident CIT withholding on dividends, interest, and royalties must be remitted within 7 days after the payment date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification, entity type, and CIT filing status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Because the FIP is pass-through, the FIP itself must not file Form A100000 as a CIT taxpayer. The Hong Kong corporate partner must declare whether it is a resident of Hong Kong for DTA purposes, whether it has a permanent establishment in Mainland China, and whether the FIP income is effectively connected to that permanent establishment. Attach the Hong Kong Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the Inland Revenue Department.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross income and revenue from all business activities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Hong Kong corporate partner must include only China-source income attributable to its partnership interest, such as franchise royalties, syrup supply chain revenue, management fees, and POS-related revenue. Foreign-source active business income should remain outside the PRC filing unless it is effectively connected with a PRC permanent establishment. Cross-border invoice recharacterization is a serious audit risk.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible business costs, operating expenses, taxes, and charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only actual and documented arm's length expenses. Disallow excessive intercompany royalties or management fees paid to a Hong Kong shell with no economic substance. Apply the PRC thin capitalization rule: interest deductions are limited by a 2:1 debt-to-equity ratio for non-financial enterprises and 5:1 for financial institutions. Related-party service charges must satisfy the benefit test and transfer pricing documentation requirements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating profit or loss computed by the FIP and allocated to partners.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The corporate partner must use the FIP profit allocation statement. If the Hong Kong partner has no permanent establishment in China, its allocated China-source profits may be taxed on a gross or deemed basis under the non-resident enterprise rules. A loss allocation to a non-resident partner without a PE generally cannot be used to reduce other China-source income and may be denied entirely.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustments: permanent differences, temporary differences, treaty income exemptions, and special tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose all DTA-related income in Schedule A107011: dividends, interest, and royalty income from the PRC side. The HK corporate partner claiming a reduced rate must attach the TRC, beneficial ownership declaration, ownership structure chart, board meeting minutes, financial statements, and evidence of core income-generating activities in Hong Kong. Without substantive business activity, the principal purpose test will deny treaty relief.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits, PRC withholding taxes, and previously paid provisional CIT.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the HK corporate partner is itself a PRC resident enterprise, it may claim foreign tax credits for taxes paid to Hong Kong. If the partner is a non-resident, any PRC withholding tax on repatriation is a final tax and must be reconciled to the treaty rate. Do not claim a foreign tax credit for the 5% treaty withholding unless the partner is filing a return as a resident enterprise.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax liability, refund or carryover adjustment, and responsible person declaration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The withholding agent must file the non-resident enterprise income tax withholding return and pay tax within 7 days of the payment. If the Hong Kong partner fails to obtain treaty relief before payment, it may apply for a refund within 3 years. The signed declaration confirms accuracy under the PRC Tax Collection Law and Criminal Law.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form A100000 may incur a penalty of RMB 2,000 under Article 62 of the PRC Tax Collection Law, increased to RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 for serious non-compliance. Late payment triggers a daily surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid tax under Article 32. Tax evasion through false declarations or fraudulent underpayment is penalized at 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax under Article 63. Criminal tax evasion under Article 201 of the PRC Criminal Law can result in imprisonment of up to 7 years for substantial evasion, plus fines, asset confiscation, travel bans, and tax-related blacklisting.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory PRC withholding tax on dividends or deemed profit distributions to non-resident corporate partners; reduced to 5% under the Mainland-Hong Kong DTA where the Hong Kong beneficial owner is a company that directly holds at least 25% of the capital of the PRC payer. Hong Kong itself does not impose any withholding tax on dividend distributions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the Hong Kong corporate partner must obtain a Certificate of Resident Status from the Hong Kong Inland Revenue Department and deliver it to the PRC withholding agent before or at the time of payment. The claimant must submit a beneficial ownership self-assessment, organizational documents, shareholding registry, board meeting minutes, staff payroll evidence, premises leases, bank records, and a statement confirming the company carries on substantive business activity and core income-generating activities in Hong Kong. The PRC tax authority applies the principal purpose test and the beneficial ownership rules under SAT Announcement 2018 No. 9. If treaty relief is denied or over-withholding occurs, the excess PRC withholding tax must be refunded through the non-resident refund procedure within 3 years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory PRC rates are 10% CIT on cross-border interest and royalties, plus 6% VAT and surcharges on taxable services. Under the Mainland-Hong Kong DTA, the withholding tax rate on royalties is 7%; interest is generally limited to 7%, with a reduced 4% rate for interest derived by Hong Kong banks or insurance companies satisfying the conditions of the Fifth Protocol. Entry fees for franchise license and trademark royalties must be carefully distinguished from taxable services, management fees, or sale of goods under transfer pricing substance principles.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: RMB 100,000,000 aggregate related-party transactions in a tax year for mandatory Local File preparation; RMB 1,000,000,000 aggregate cross-border related-party transactions for mandatory Master File preparation.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Mainland-Hong Kong DTA benefit requires the Hong Kong partner to have real economic substance in Hong Kong, including substantive board decisions, local management, employees, premises, and the performance of core income-generating activities in Hong Kong. The PRC tax authorities may invoke the General Anti-Avoidance Rule under Article 47 of the PRC CIT Law and the principal purpose test to deny treaty benefits where an FIP or Hong Kong affiliate is a conduit or shell. For Hong Kong profits tax purposes, offshore sourcing and any preferential claims require evidence that the franchise licensing functions, trademark management, pricing decisions, and key business risks are located in Hong Kong.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Hong Kong partner is a letterbox company that claims the 5% DTA dividend rate on profits from the PRC boba tea franchise while having no employees, no premises, no bank account, and no independent decision-making. The Hong Kong company is used solely as a conduit to extract profits and route them to individual mainland owners, while the PRC withholding agent underwithholds tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority will deny the DTA benefit and impose the full 10% statutory withholding rate. For under-declaration, Article 63 of the PRC Tax Collection Law imposes a penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax plus daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05%. If the case is criminalized under Article 201 of the PRC Criminal Law, the responsible individuals face fines and imprisonment up to 7 years for tax evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and actual controllers who control the Hong Kong conduit can have the corporate veil pierced under PRC Company Law principles: they become jointly and severally liable for the underpaid PRC withholding tax, civil restitution of the fraudulent tax benefit, and any late surcharge. They also face tax blacklisting, exit restrictions, travel bans, and potential criminal imprisonment of 3 to 7 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The PRC franchise operating entity pays a 20% of gross sales trademark royalty to the Hong Kong partner, but the trademark was developed by mainland employees, the Hong Kong entity performs no substantive brand management, and the profit margin of the PRC entity falls below 1%. No contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation is prepared despite related-party transactions exceeding the statutory threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The PRC tax authority may make a transfer pricing adjustment under Article 41 of the CIT Law, disallow the excessive royalty deduction, reallocate taxable profit to the PRC entity, and impose interest and late-payment surcharges. Failure to prepare the Local File may attract penalties under Article 44 of the Tax Collection Law of RMB 10,000 to RMB 50,000. If the adjustment is treated as tax evasion, the penalty escalates to 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false intercompany agreements, control the royalty pricing, and cause the underpayment of tax are at risk of personal joint and several liability for the adjusted tax, interest, and penalties. Asset restitution orders, freezing of personal bank accounts, travel bans, and director disqualification can be imposed. Criminal prosecution under Article 201 of the Criminal Law can result in up to 7 years imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The global boba tea franchise routes POS cash, franchise fees, and syrup supply payments through the FIP using informal Hong Kong payment rails, issues false VAT invoices for fictitious management consulting, and intentionally hides the true amount of royalty income from the PRC tax authority.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The conduct violates the PRC Anti-Money Laundering Law and Article 191 of the Criminal Law, which imposes asset confiscation and imprisonment of up to 10 years for money laundering. Issuing false VAT invoices violates Article 205 of the Criminal Law, carrying fines and imprisonment up to life imprisonment in severe cases. The Tax Collection Law imposes additional penalties of 50% to 500% of the evaded tax and daily late-payment surcharges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and partners cannot hide behind the pass-through FIP structure. The general partner bears unlimited joint and several liability for the partnership's unpaid taxes and civil restitution. Personal assets may be frozen and confiscated. Directors face criminal prosecution for money laundering and tax evasion with combined imprisonment exposure of up to 10 years, plus travel bans and blacklisting from the financial system.
